record.paper_title: Neutrino theory: open questions and future opportunities
record.original_question: Are neutrinos Dirac fermions or Majorana fermions, and what new physics is required in either case to generate their masses consistently with the Standard Model gauge structure? If neutrinos are Majorana particles, the theory must explain the new degrees of freedom and lepton-number-violating mechanism responsible for Majorana masses; if they are Dirac particles, the theory must explain the presence of right-handed neutrinos and the principle that forbids renormalizable Majorana mass terms for those right-handed states.

evidence.quote: When made massive, neutrinos are either Dirac or Majorana fermions. If they are Majorana fermions, then they are the first such elementary particles discovered, and thus constitute New Physics (NP). There are a very large number of viable mechanisms for generating Majorana masses, and they all involve new degrees of freedom.

If, on the other hand, neutrinos are Dirac fermions, then RH neutrinos are needed. They are new degrees of freedom and hence NP. Also, in the context of the SM gauge group, the renormalisable and gauge-invariant Majorana mass terms for the RH neutrinos have to be expelled from the Lagrangian, which constitutes a new model-building principle: the imposition of global total lepton number symmetry. No matter what, ν mass requires NP.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Within the framework of the Standard Model of particle physics with gauge group SU(3)_C × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y and its three generations of left-handed lepton doublets, determine the nature of the neutrino mass term. Specifically, decide between the following two alternatives and provide the required extension of the Standard Model in each case:

(a) Majorana neutrinos. Assume the observed light neutrinos are Majorana fermions, i.e., each neutrino mass eigenstate ν satisfies ν = ν^c, so that the mass term violates total lepton number by two units. Identify the new degrees of freedom (e.g., heavy right-handed singlets, scalar triplets, fermionic triplets, higher-dimensional operators such as the Weinberg operator (LH)(LH)/Λ, etc.) and the lepton-number-violating mechanism that produces the Majorana mass matrix consistent with current oscillation and cosmological constraints.

(b) Dirac neutrinos. Assume instead that neutrinos are Dirac fermions, so that distinct right-handed singlet states ν_R must be added to the Standard Model field content. Since gauge invariance under SU(3)_C × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y permits a renormalizable Majorana mass term (1/2) M ν_R^T C ν_R for these singlets, specify the symmetry principle or model-building mechanism (e.g., an exact global total lepton number U(1)_L, a discrete subgroup thereof, or a geometric/extra-dimensional origin) that forbids this term to all relevant orders, and explain how the small observed Dirac Yukawa couplings y_ν ~ m_ν / v ≲ 10^{-12} can be generated naturally.

Decide which alternative (a) or (b) is realized in nature, and exhibit the minimal consistent new physics required.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana fermions remains one of the major open problems in particle physics. Neutrinoless double-beta decay experiments (KamLAND-Zen, LEGEND, CUORE, nEXO) continue to search for the lepton-number-violating signal that would establish the Majorana nature, but as of 2026 no positive signal has been reported. Numerous theoretical mechanisms (seesaw of various types, radiative models, Dirac-mass models with enforced lepton number) remain viable.

status_evidence.title: KamLAND-Zen latest limit on neutrinoless double-beta decay
status_evidence.snippet: KamLAND-Zen reports a lower limit on the 0νββ half-life of 136Xe, constraining the effective Majorana mass but finding no signal.
status_evidence.claim: No experimental evidence yet establishes the Majorana nature of neutrinos; the Dirac-vs-Majorana question is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino theory: open questions and future opportunities
status_evidence.snippet: Whether neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana is listed as a foremost open question; both possibilities require new physics beyond the Standard Model.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is identified as open in recent neutrino-theory reviews.
